revised_claim_text: Indonesia had approximately 6.1 million registered trucks (commercial freight vehicles) as of end-2023, out of 157 million total registered motor vehicles (BPS, updated Feb 2024). The 23M+ figure cited by Mordor Intelligence almost certainly refers to total non-motorcycle motor vehicles (~24.6M = cars + trucks + buses) or a broader 'commercial vehicle fleet' definition inclusive of motorcycles used for commercial delivery; it does not represent the freight truck fleet. The 4–5M Kemenhub figure (no URL) is directionally consistent but understates the BPS-confirmed 6.09M truck count and should be updated. For fleet/telematics purposes, the correct addressable market is approximately 6 million trucks.
notes: Disambiguation confirmed: BPS classifies Indonesia's registered vehicles into four categories — sepeda motor (motorcycles, 132.4M), mobil penumpang (passenger cars, 18.3M), truk (trucks, 6.09M), bis (buses, 270K). The ~6M truck figure is the commercially relevant freight/goods vehicle fleet. The 23M Mordor figure cannot be reconciled with any single BPS category; it is most likely (a) total non-motorcycle vehicles ~24.6M, rounded down or from an earlier year, or (b) a broader definition including all 'commercial use' vehicles (motorcycles on ride-hail/delivery platforms + trucks + buses), which would be misleading for fleet telematics market sizing. The Kemenhub HUBNET portal (hubnet.kemenhub.go.id/dataset/content/dataset/30) has annual data in Excel/JSON through 2024; the 2024 figure is expected to be ~6.2–6.4M trucks. Recommend: unify both VC-42 and PP3.3-3 to '~6M registered trucks (BPS 2023)' and retire the Mordor 23M figure as methodologically unverified for this context.
